title: Quantification of skull-skin-vibrations during bone conduction stimulation at the hearing threshold by Laser-Doppler-Vibrometry
summary:
In this study, we want to investigate the effect of fine vibrations on the head (generated by a bone conduction headphone) on skin vibrations in different parts of the head. This technique is used, among other things, for people who have difficulty hearing normally (i.e., through air conduction).
We use a high-precision laser device (laser Doppler vibrometer) to measure how strongly the skin vibrates at different points on the head when exposed to very quiet sound stimulation. We do this by directing a harmless laser beam at a small area behind the ear or at other points on the skull. These measurements are non-contact and painless.
Adults between the ages of 18 and 39 with a normal BMI and no relevant pre-existing conditions or head surgery are included.
We want to find out whether the skin vibrations triggered by sound stimulation are similarly strong in all individuals (regardless of gender or individual characteristics) and whether they are related to the volume of the sounds played. In the long term, this may help to develop new bone conduction systems.
In a second part of the study, we are also testing a novel hearing system that works entirely without touching the skin: a laser beam generates fine vibrations directly at the auricle, which are then transmitted to the inner ear in a similar way to a bone conduction headphone. We want to find out whether the skin vibrations generated by this laser system can be measured just as reliably, and how strong they need to be for a tone to be just barely audible. For this part of the study, healthy adults between the ages of 18 and 29 with normal hearing are included.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- BMI within the normal range (between 18.5 and 24.9 kg/m²)
- Written and spoken German language skills

additional inclusion criteria for cohort 2 (photoacoustic stimulation)
- Age between 18 and 29 years
- bone conduction threshold (right ear): below 10 dB HL
- air conduction threshold (right ear): below 10 dB HL
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to give consent or consent to participate in the study
- Known pregnancy (anamnestic)
- Tattoos, injuries, (large) scars, or piercings in the skull area around the ear (exception: auricle), on the lower jaw, or on the forehead
- Active skin diseases in which the mechanical tissue properties of the skin in the measurement area are altered (e.g., sunburn, neurodermatitis, psoriasis)
- Skin disease in which the application of a (reflective) patch is contraindicated.
- Known disease of the endocrine system (anamnestic) that can influence the mechanical properties of the skin (e.g., estrogen deficiency).
- Major skeletal abnormalities in the skull area (e.g., previous fractures, operations)
- Diseases that lead to changes in bone density (e.g., osteoporosis).
